markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's own logged Cycle Explorer readings (a day with its lining thickness or percentage, e.g. thin on day 1-5 and thick around day 22) as evidence.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine day/lining pairs from the student's own Investigation Record rows; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('the lining gets thicker') with no actual logged readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that the lining thickens after the period (rebuilt in the first half and kept thick in the second half) to prepare for a possible pregnancy, and names a hormone that controls this (oestrogen rebuilds it; progesterone keeps it thick).
markingScheme.accept: Any valid phrasing of the lining thickening/building up under oestrogen and/or progesterone; either hormone earns the point.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying the lining 'changes' with no direction, purpose or hormone named.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why a period happens: if the egg is not fertilised, progesterone (and oestrogen) fall, so the thick lining breaks down and leaves the body as a period.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that without fertilisation the lining breaks down and is shed; mention of falling hormones strengthens but is not required if the cause (no fertilisation) is clear.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'a period is blood' or 'it happens every month' with no link to no fertilisation or the lining breaking down.

markingScheme.criterion: States that Ana (first period at 10) and Mia (not yet at 12) are both within normal variation, because periods usually begin anywhere from about 9 to 15 and bodies start puberty at different times.
markingScheme.accept: Any statement that a wide range of start ages is normal, covering both an early and a later starter.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'it is normal' with no reference to a range or to people differing.

markingScheme.criterion: States that Zoe's 32-day cycle is normal because 28 days is only an average and healthy cycles vary (roughly 21-35 days).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that cycle length varies and 32 days is within the healthy range.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying Zoe's cycle is 'broken' or 'wrong', or simply 'it is fine' with no reason.

markingScheme.criterion: Names a sensible person to talk to if still worried (parent or carer, school nurse, teacher or doctor) AND gives a reason it is sensible (e.g. cycles can be irregular in the first years, or a doctor can check that everything is healthy).
markingScheme.accept: Any appropriate trusted adult or health professional with a brief reason.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming a person with no reason, or suggesting asking only friends or the internet.
